page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for cost-efficient compute and memory balance. The instance provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES-NI, SHA extensions, and BMI2, while advanced AVX-512 extensions and AMX units are absent. The configuration does not include local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations position the e2-standard-16 across median industry tiers for general-purpose workloads. In computational testing, the instance achieved a multi-core score of 21,462.05 on stress-ng and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 9,337.0, supported by a single-core score of 1,486.0. Memory bandwidth results reach 113.16 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 60.92 GB/sec for large block writes. In specialized operational benchmarks, the instance completed 10.37 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 8.31 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. For lightweight artificial intelligence tasks, the machine sustained 751.67 tokens per second for prompt processing and 198.93 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M parameter model.

From an infrastructure perspective, the e2-standard-16 targets operational efficiency by delivering steady multi-threaded capacity without the overhead of specialized hardware. The primary tradeoff lies in the lack of bundled local storage and the absence of hardware accelerators such as GPUs or AVX-512 vector pipelines, limiting its capability for heavy matrix computing or direct local I/O intensive setups. The instance profile is suited for enterprise web serving, mid-sized relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration build pipelines, and general business applications.

The configuration operates with 8 physical cores at 2 threads per core, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU without bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results demonstrate stable, median-tier performance across multi-core computing and memory operations, recording a PassMark CPU score of 21,986.39, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,337.0, and 10.37 million Redis SET operations per second. Supported CPU instruction sets include AVX, AES, and SHA extensions. The instance offers a balanced ratio of compute and memory, making it well fitted for enterprise web serving, compilation pipelines, in-memory caching systems, and general production workloads.
